source: Chief Architect X18 Tutorial Guide, Interior Design Tutorials, pages 191-210

steps.step: Library: a 'Beach Palette' folder in the User Catalog with five paint colours copied in
(User Catalog folders; copy from the core catalog)
steps.gap: Paint colours are made as plan materials; there's no shipped colour catalog to copy from, and library folders hold objects, not plan materials. Row: LIB-01

steps.step: Wall finish for every room: Color - Butter
Material Eyedropper on a Butter wall; the Garage's walls Color - Fresh (Room Specification > Materials)
Material Painter in Room mode: the Bedroom walls Color - Dew
Object mode: one wall (Dining/Bedroom... here the Living/Bedroom wall) Color - Maya Gold
Select a wall in 3D with Select Next Object (Tab); its interior surfaces show No Change across three rooms
steps.gap: Walls have one material per side, not one per room they face. Row: MAT-31

steps.step: Wall covering: white beadboard wainscot 48" high in the Dining room
steps.gap: No wall coverings (a finish layer over part of a room's walls); use a wall material region. Row: MAT-32

steps.step: Wall material region defaults: tile on backerboard, cutting the wall's finish
steps.gap: Material regions are a material on the surface, not layers that cut the wall's finish. Row: WL-16

steps.step: Wall Elevation of the Bath's left wall; a tile region on it, 18" up from the floor, 12" below the ceiling
(Wall Elevation view of one room's wall; Simplify Polyline; Reflect About Object for the opposite wall)
steps.gap: No single-wall elevation view; regions are edited in their specification, not drawn in an elevation. Row: SEC-14

steps.step: Flooring: red oak plank everywhere (Floor/Ceiling Platform floor finish); room types keep their own
